idiom_name: immutable bindings + shared references &T (Arc for sharing)
implementation_notes: Immutability is the default mode of the language rather than a pattern applied to it: a let binding cannot be reassigned without mut, a shared reference &T gives read-only access, and the borrowing rules allow any number of &T or exactly one &mut T, so aliasing and mutation cannot coexist. Sharing then means putting the value behind Arc (or referring to it with 'static) and never handing out &mut; interior mutability (Cell, RefCell, Mutex, atomics) is the explicit, locally visible escape hatch and appears in the type. For value-like data, derive Clone and return new values from methods that take &self.
pitfalls: Interior mutability defeats the guarantee quietly at run time: RefCell borrows are checked dynamically and a conflicting borrow panics, while Cell and RefCell are not Sync, so they cannot be shared across threads without a lock.

Sharing an immutable value across threads needs Send + Sync plus Arc; a struct containing Rc or RefCell loses Sync even though it looks immutable, and the error appears at the use site rather than the definition.
Immutable bindings do not stop mutation reached through a &mut obtained elsewhere or through UnsafeCell; the guarantee is the borrow checker's enforcement, not a runtime property of the value.
